review_notes: I read the whole target file and the Series API in Definitions/Def_CerednikDrinfeld_SpecialFormalModule.lean (lines 24–28, 134–164). The file declares no simp lemmas itself, so my findings concern the simp interface it depends on. I grepped that definitions file for `comp_apply` and `id_apply` and found nothing. I did not search the rest of the repo or Mathlib, so a lemma elsewhere could cover these. I did not run Lean, so I don't know whether the proposed lemmas close these goals by `simp` or whether they would clash with other rules.

findings.declaration: NilpCoords.map_span_range_eq (and solution.h2, which has the same pattern)
findings.problem: `Series.comp` and `Series.id` are plain `def`s with no pointwise simp or rfl lemmas (`Series.comp_apply`, `Series.id_apply`). To get from `(ψ.comp φ) j` to `subst φ (ψ j)`, the proofs use `show ... = _`, defeq `rfl`, and `congrFun huv i`, which silently unfolds the definition. This depends on `Series.comp` being unfolded by hand at each use, and `simp` cannot normalise these terms. Line 110 has the same pattern: `have hx : MvPowerSeries.subst v (u i) = MvPowerSeries.X i := congrFun huv i` relies on `(Series.id B) i` unfolding to `X i`.
findings.proposed_change: In the definitions file, next to `Series.comp` and `Series.id`, add `@[simp] theorem Series.comp_apply (ψ φ : Series B) (i : Fin 2) : (ψ.comp φ) i = MvPowerSeries.subst φ (ψ i) := rfl` and `@[simp] theorem Series.id_apply (i : Fin 2) : Series.id B i = MvPowerSeries.X i := rfl`. Then the `show` steps and the `rfl` / `congrFun` coercions can become `simp [Series.comp_apply]` or `rw [Series.comp_apply]`.
findings.benefit: Every pointwise statement about `Series` composition then normalises to the `subst` form that Mathlib's `MvPowerSeries.subst` lemmas expect. Proofs no longer depend on `show` and defeq unfolding, and they keep working if the representation of `Series.comp` changes.

evidence.excerpt: def Series.comp (ψ φ : Series B) : Series B := fun i => subst φ (ψ i)
def Series.id (B : Type u) [CommRing B] : Series B := fun i => MvPowerSeries.X i

findings.excerpt: rw [Series.comp_assoc φ u v hu0 hv0, huv, Series.comp_id]
findings.problem: `Series.comp_id` is an unconditional identity, `φ.comp (Series.id B) = φ`, but it is not tagged `@[simp]`. Its sibling `Series.map_id` is `@[simp]`, and the file applies `comp_id` by manual `rw`. Because `Series.id_comp` needs a constant-coefficient hypothesis, it cannot be a plain simp lemma. This leaves an asymmetric API: the unconditional rule is not available to `simp`, so `Series.comp φ (Series.id B)` terms are not normalised automatically.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `Series.comp_id` as `@[simp]` in the definitions file. Optionally also state `Series.id_comp` with the hypothesis as a simp-dischargeable argument, which is how `simp` would use it.
findings.benefit: Terms like `φ.comp (Series.id B)` would be normalised automatically. The rewrite is terminating and non-looping because the right-hand side `φ` is strictly smaller, and the unconditional orientation is canonical. Proofs like `hcomp` could then end with `simp [huv]` instead of a hand-ordered `rw` chain.

evidence.excerpt: theorem Series.comp_id (φ : Series B) : φ.comp (Series.id B) = φ := by
@[simp] theorem Series.map_id (f : B →+* B') : (Series.id B).map f = Series.id B' := by
